DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis).

Although the ESR/CRP were normal and fundoscopy was unremarkable, the combination of new-onset headache, progressive visual loss, vascular risk factors, and the specific request for visual evoked potentials strongly suggests an inflammatory vasculopathy affecting the ophthalmic artery; a temporal artery biopsy is urgently required to confirm this diagnosis and prevent permanent blindness.
